newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK tycoon blasts Lee, Patten for "untruths".
newsitem.headline: HK tycoon blasts Lee, Patten for "untruths".

text.p: One of Hong Kong's richest property magnates accused outgoing governor Chris Patten on Thursday of spreading lies about the territory.

Ronnie Chan, chairman of property giant Hang Lung Development Co, also took a swipe at the territory's best known democracy activist, Martin Lee, for painting a black picture of Hong Kong's prospects under Chinese rule.

Chan slammed Patten for an article he wrote for Newsweek magazine in March criticising the Chinese-appointed Provisional Legislature, which takes over from Hong Kong's current elected Legislative Council when Britain hands the territory back on July 1.
"I believe Chris Patten's article in Newsweek on March 3 is full of untruths," Chan said, noting that Patten refers to the Provisional Legislature meeting "furtively" across the border in China.

"A foreign reader would think Hong Kong people are up in arms against the Provisional Legislature. A lot of people are against the Provisional Legislature, but there are a lot of people who are not against the Provisional Legislature," he said.
Chan cited a recent survey noting that 67 percent of Hong Kong had accepted the Provisional Legislature.
The outspoken tycoon also took aim at Lee, leader of Hong Kong's popular Democratic Party, the largest in the outgoing legislature.
Chan said that worries were normal during a time of historic transition, but that Lee's vocal courtship of Washington D.C. was at odds with his more toned-down approach back in Hong Kong.
Lee earlier this year secured a promise from U.S. President Bill Clinton that the United States would watch out for freedom and liberty in Hong Kong.
"I do believe what Martin Lee is doing is very harmful to Hong Kong," said Chan.
Forbes Magazine named Chan, 46, among the world's 400 richest individuals in both 1995 and 1996.
Born in Hong Kong, Chan serves on the boards of a number of overseas-listed companies, including Standard Chartered Plc and Enron Corp.
He is also on the World Economic Forum (WEF) council.
